stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M, but why?
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured a $190 million Series C funding round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This capital influx emphasizes the growing importance of co-orbital security and space domain awareness (SDA) as the Department of Defense increasingly looks to private firms for technological solutions. The funding suggests that investors are betting heavily on the DoD's appetite for commercial partnerships.
stories.soWhat: If you're not in the co-orbital security game, you're probably missing out on the next wave of government contracts.

stories.head: Vantor picks BAE for next-gen satellites.
stories.body: Vantor has chosen BAE Systems to develop its next-generation imaging satellites, marking a reunion reminiscent of the DigitalGlobe era. This partnership highlights a trend where established players are turning to familiar faces in the industry to mitigate risks associated with new tech development. Financial terms were not disclosed, but the strategic alignment hints at a long-term vision for enhanced imaging capabilities.
stories.soWhat: When companies play it safe with known partners, it tells you they’re prioritizing reliability over novelty in a volatile market.

stories.head: York Space Systems talks satellite chat.
stories.body: York Space Systems has successfully demonstrated two-way UHF communications from low Earth orbit for the U.S. Space Force. This achievement underscores the operational need for satellites to communicate effectively, especially as military operations become increasingly reliant on real-time data. The demonstration not only validates York's technology but also reinforces the Space Force's commitment to enhancing satellite communication capabilities.
stories.soWhat: In a world where data is king, even satellites need to gossip to stay relevant.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's next moves.
watchlist.body: With fresh capital, True Anomaly could ramp up its development and partnerships, potentially reshaping the co-orbital security landscape.

watchlist.title: Watch for BAE's new satellite capabilities.
watchlist.body: BAE's work with Vantor could set new standards in imaging technology, influencing future contracts and partnerships.

watchlist.title: Anticipate more from York Space Systems.
watchlist.body: York's successful communications demo may lead to more contracts with the Space Force, as the need for reliable satellite communication grows.

watchlist.title: Monitor the hypersonic testing delays.
watchlist.body: Continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests could indicate deeper issues in defense tech development, affecting budget allocations.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.

tickers.note: Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN program shows that government contracts are still lucrative, albeit slow-moving.
Astranis' $250M funding round for microGEO production capital hints at a serious play in the small satellite market.
Stoke Space's $260M Series C indicates investor confidence in fully reusable launch systems, but execution remains key.
K2 Space's $110M Series B funding reflects a growing demand for high-power satellites in national security missions.
